extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: The first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis, featuring 900 videos across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, varying durations, and 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Raw videos were sourced from YouTube based on a domain hierarchy of 6 key domains and 30 subfields. Videos with varying duration lengths (short, medium, long) were collected, along with corresponding subtitles (if provided) and audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios, indicating missing subtitles for 156 videos.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro. Questions not meeting the video-content requirement were returned for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator viewed the entire video and created three relevant multiple-choice questions with four candidate options. A quality review was conducted where a different annotator verified language clarity, logical consistency, and answer appropriateness. Additionally, text-only questions answerable by Gemini 1.5 Pro were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, ensuring questions require video content. The distribution of options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Long videos exhibit a long-tailed distribution, with fewer samples as the duration increases. Shorter videos predominantly involve perception-related tasks, while longer videos mainly feature tasks related to reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases. Restricted input frames can become an information bottleneck for understanding the full content of long videos. The long-tailed distribution of data poses challenges for acquisition.
